question: Holding surviving donors' marginal local failure probability fixed, can reduced synchronization compensate for loss of one donor, and how does source-to-target arrival success change the sign?

references.paper: Fox et al. 2017 Nat Ecol Evol
references.documented_result: Transient local catastrophic extinctions, habitat intact, can reduce synchrony and increase metapopulation persistence under high dispersal and cyclic protist predator/prey dynamics

references.paper: Matter & Roland 2010 Proc R Soc B
references.documented_result: Experimental removal of two adjacent butterfly local populations in a 17-population network decreased immigration and increased synchrony in nearby residual populations; no direct experimentally demonstrated eventual metapopulation extinction effect

synthetic_state_model.common_catastrophe: One Bernoulli(c) event forces all n donor failures. Otherwise donor failures iid Bernoulli(p), p=(q-c)/(1-c), so each donor's unconditional failure probability is q.
synthetic_state_model.source_to_target_arrival: Each viable donor independently produces >=1 effective arrival with Bernoulli(a), independent conditional on viability; no dispersal-distance geometry modeled.
synthetic_state_model.endpoint: Whether ZERO successful arrivals reach ONE target in ONE period, not metapopulation extinction or recolonization
synthetic_state_model.equal_marginal_failure: Each donor fixed q before/after; expected viable donor count decreases with n
synthetic_state_model.solve: Nonzero root for P_after(no arrival)=P_before(no arrival), positive bracket [.1,1], 90-step bisection; include no-common-shock counterfactual and predeclared a grid
synthetic_state_model.known_truth_validation: Enumerate every local donor viability vector for n<=5 and verify exact formula independently within float tolerance 1e-13

epistemic_limits: This is a stylized mechanism existence witness, not newly discovered empirical result
Fox experimental transient patch reset cannot be equated with lasting loss of an occupied island
Matter butterfly synchrony increase is prior published, but it did not experimentally demonstrate later global extinction
Neither common-shock c nor per-survivor target dispersal success a is inferred from real experiment data
Original Structural v1.123 source-loss leverage hypothesis remains future-only; this does not change its confirmation or outcome exposure
Do not market opposite results as contradictory: intervention permanence, density heterogeneity, predator cycles, dispersal and external shock processes differ
Source count and covariance are necessary to define temporal risk, but this model does not identify which source island to protect
All original mammal heldout responses and GEB scientific HOLD intact, eBird excluded
source_data_candidate: Fox 2017 DOI 10.5061/dryad.2rs23 contains experiment raw CSV and README; data not accessed in analytical model
